sentences.text: Prosecution case, in brief, is that on 01.07.2023 at about 16:30 - 16:40 hours, applicant entered into the house of the prosecutrix, gagged her mouth and forcefully took her inside the room and sexually assaulted her.

Learned counsel for the applicant referring to the FIR bearing Crime No.171/2023 lodged by the applicant on the date of incident at the same Police Station at about 18:40 hours submits that on the date of incident at about 17:30 - 17:40 hours, when he was going for answering the nature's call, complainant and her husband both on previous enmity abused him and when he objected, complainant's husband assaulted with wooden stick on frontal side of the head and left while prosecutrix assaulted with wooden stick on left hand of the applicant, due to which, he sustained injuries.

After lodging of above FIR,
complainant lodged a false and fabricated report against the applicant.

He further submits that prior to the incident, on 07.09.2020 complainant's husband along with other co-accused assaulted him,
about which he lodged FIR bearing Crime No.285/2020 against him, whereafter complainant's mother-in-law lodged FIR bearing Crime No.76/2021 on 25.03.2021 against the applicant for offence punishable under Sections 323, 294, 506 of IPC.
Thus, the applicant's relation with the complainant are strained, due to which, as a counterblast of the applicant's FIR, forged and fabricated case has been made against him.
Trial will take time to conclude, therefore, he is entitled for bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer.
Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.

Upon perusal of the case diary, it appears that on the date of incident at about 13:50 hours, MLC of the applicant was conducted wherein injury was found on his head and, therefore, under these circumstances and considering the material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant, so also the other facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.
It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
This application is allowed and stands disposed of.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Abhi Gauri Shankar Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6313167/
